title: Box the Trait
goal: Store circles and squares in one Vec. Wrap them the way trait objects require.
hints: dyn Draw has no fixed size - the compiler can't put 'some unknown shape' directly in a Vec.
Behind a Box, every trait object is one pointer wide. Box the circle, box the square.
explanation: A Vec needs elements of one known size, but Circle and Square are different types - the escape is dynamic dispatch: Box<dyn Draw> is a fat pointer (data + vtable), uniform in size, calling the right draw() at runtime. Bare dyn Draw is unsized and can't live in a Vec directly (E0277), and Vec<Circle> simply can't hold a Square. This is the genuine use case for dyn: heterogeneous collections. When everything's the same type, prefer generics - monomorphization is free.
